messages:
jess: Heads up — after the quant4b-v2 bringup we saw a ~4.6% drop in embedding recall on the anchor/golden holdout. Looks concentrated in paraphrase-heavy buckets. Can we triage coverage fallout and decide whether to roll back or patch?

sam: Ugh. Do we have a minimal repro and the eval command?

jess: Repro is here — ran our weighted-anchor eval against holdout_v3. Command I used: `python tools/eval/compare_holdouts.py --model quant4b-v2 --gold holdout_v3 --out /tmp/q4b-holdout-report.json`

elaine: Can you paste the top failure examples? A few quick checks: 1) are these duplicates that slipped into the holdout? 2) did tokenization change after quantization? 3) are we seeing KL/regression or just recall delta? :eyes:

jess: Pasting a couple snippets (sanitized):

```
Query: "How do I transfer my subscription to a different email?"
Gold: "To transfer a subscription, contact billing with both emails."
Model: "To transfer, go to settings -> account -> transfer" (incorrect, hallucinated flow)
\nQuery: "Best way to rephrase 'I'm locked out of my account' for support"
Gold: "I can't access my account, please help"
Model: "How can I reset my password?" (missed the escalation intent)
```

jess: These look like paraphrase collapse + intent shift, which explains recall hit more than token-level metrics.

sam: Thanks. If it's paraphrase collapse we should run fingerprint/dedup diffs between the pre-quant holdout and post-quant examples to rule out contamination. Command: `tools/ingest/fingerprint_diff.sh holdout_v2 holdout_v3 > /tmp/fp-diff.txt`

mike: I kicked off a fingerprint job (`job-89321`) to recompute embeddings/fingerprints for both holdouts & the seedbank. ETA ~18m. I also pinned the model route to quant4b-v1 for dedicated traffic to avoid user impact.

anya: I can triage the golden labels for the affected anchors. If we need a relabel, I can spin up a 50-case batch focused on paraphrase/intent mismatches. ETA to first batch: ~2hrs. Do we want full relabel or just QA?

elaine: Start with targeted relabel/QA on the top 200 failure anchors (by delta). If relabel rate > 15% then escalate to full relabel. Also add a synthetic paraphrase augmentation to the holdout to catch this class earlier.

jess: Agreed. Sam/elaine — can you produce the top-200 list and the delta breakdown? I'll attach to the labeling task and link to examples.

sam: Yep — will run `scripts/anchor_delta/top_k_failures.py --report /tmp/q4b-holdout-report.json --k 200 --out /tmp/top200.json` and push to the shared drive.

qa-bot: automated-run: eval/regression-check triggered for quant4b-v2 against holdout_v3 — summary: recall -4.6%, precision stable, avg token change +0.2. Full report: https://internal/reports/q4b-v2-holdout (internal)

mike: fingerprint job finished; diff shows ~12 collisions added to holdout_v3 (likely from samplebank dedupe bug). Results uploaded to `/artifacts/fp-diff-2419876543.txt`.

anya: I'll prioritize the top200 and flag any that look like contamination vs true model regression. If contaminated, we can remove from holdout and rerun. I'll post a checklist in 1.5h.

jess: Plan then: (1) Sam produces top-200 + delta by 30m, (2) Mike confirms any contamination list and we remove contaminated anchors, (3) Anya runs targeted QA/relabel on remaining anchors, (4) Elaine adds synthetic paraphrase augmentation + run quick quant-smoke. If relabel >15% or regression persists after cleanup -> rollback.

sam: On it.

elaine: I'll also add a small eval harness to measure paraphrase robustness specifically: `pytest tests/eval/test_paraphrase_robustness.py::test_quant4b_paraphrase` — should help catch this earlier.

mike: Noted. I'll hold the rollback window open until 4h from now. :thumbsup:

jess: Thanks everyone. Posting updates here as they come. :raised_hands:
